extracted.intended_audience: general readers, viewers, and researchers interested in the documentary series
extracted.subtask_description: A Wikipedia article summarizing the 2022 Showtime documentary miniseries 'We Need to Talk About Cosby', including production details, episode summaries, reception, controversies, and awards. Useful for readers seeking an encyclopedic overview of the series.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rotten Tomatoes score and consensus
rubrics_metrics.description: On the review aggregator website Rotten Tomatoes, 99% of 69 critics' reviews are positive, with an average rating of 8.5/10. The website's consensus reads: "W. Kamau Bell deftly unpacks the Cosby scandal by allowing the conversation to be uncomfortable, yielding a robust examination of the disgraced entertainer and the culture that enabled him."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rotten Tomatoes provides percent positive and average rating; the consensus statement summarizes key strengths critics cite (e.g., willingness to be uncomfortable, robust cultural examination). Use percent_positive + average_rating + consensus to summarize critical approval and characteristic praise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Metacritic weighted average score
rubrics_metrics.description: Metacritic, which uses a weighted average, assigned the series a score of 83 out of 100 based on 22 critics, indicating "universal acclaim."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Metacritic's weighted score and descriptive banding (e.g., 'universal acclaim') serve as a quantitative indicator of critical reception; note the sample size (number of critics) and the fact that weighting affects the aggregated score.

rubrics_metrics.name: U.S. viewership per episode
rubrics_metrics.description: Episode-level U.S. viewers (millions) are listed for each of the four episodes (e.g., Part 1: 0.166 million; Part 2: 0.184 million; Part 3: 0.126 million; Part 4: 0.145 million).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Episode viewership numbers indicate audience reach on initial broadcast; compare across episodes to track retention. Treat small fractional millions as raw Nielsen/Showbuzz-style estimates and consider on-demand/streaming numbers separately if available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Festival premiere and release strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: The series had its world premiere at the 2022 Sundance Film Festival on January 22, 2022, and was released on January 30, 2022, on Showtime.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Festival premieres (e.g., Sundance) signal prestige and can affect critical attention; release timing and platform (premium cable/streaming) shape audience expectations and distribution reach. Notes mention some episodes were made available on Showtime's on-demand/streaming platforms ahead of weekly premieres.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentary subject scope and method
rubrics_metrics.description: The series "explores the life and career of Bill Cosby up to his sexual assault cases, through conversations with comedians, journalists, and survivors."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate scope by how comprehensively the series covers life, career, and allegations, and by the range of interviewees (comics, journalists, survivors). Inclusion of survivors and domain experts is a key criterion for documentary thoroughness and credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of the subject's response
rubrics_metrics.description: A representative for Cosby issued a statement prior to the premiere denying all allegations and criticizing the film and its director ('Mr. Cosby vehemently denies all allegations...').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Including the subject's response demonstrates effort to present multiple perspectives; assess whether the response is presented in full context and whether it materially affects balance or reception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of controversial contributor remarks / ethical considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Following the documentary's airing on BBC, many took issue with a statement from contributor Sonalee Rashatwar claiming a consensual way to do what Cosby did existed and that 'sex negativity' is largely responsible for these situations, which many condemned as promoting rape culture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess ethical responsibility in representation: how the film frames, challenges, or contextualizes contentious remarks; potential for harm or criticism (e.g., accusations of promoting rape culture) is an important evaluative dimension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Awards, nominations and industry recognition
rubrics_metrics.description: The series received multiple accolades and nominations (e.g., 2022 Peabody Award — Documentary honoree (Won); Black Reel Awards for Television — Outstanding Television Documentary or Special (Won); Cinema Eye Honours nominations/wins; Critics' Choice Documentary Awards nomination; Gotham Independent Film Awards (Won); various Emmy nominations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Awards and nominations are signals of industry recognition and perceived quality; list wins vs. nominations and note the prestige/criteria of each awarding body when using awards as an evaluative metric.

rubrics_metrics.name: Production and format specifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Production details: Genre — Documentary; Directed and produced by W. Kamau Bell; Number of episodes — 4; Running time — 58–60 minutes; Production companies — Showtime Documentary Films, Boardwalk Pictures, WKB Industries; Original network — Showtime.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Production specs influence expectations for pacing, depth, and production values. Number of episodes and running time affect narrative scope; production companies and network can indicate budget and editorial stance.
